source.title: BanditRLlib Statement-Seal, Source Proof Graph, and Purification protocol

target: Make source-facing theorem interfaces immutable before proof search; separate exhaustive source-proof topology from Lean implementation topology; represent alternative proofs as OR-routes; and require post-merge purification into a compressed Bandit/RL spine.

searched_existing: BanditRLlib AGENTS.md, theorem publication protocol, semantic round trip, Lean Graph, Functor Hypergraph, contribution contract
Samplinglib source-fidelity, shared-leaf, graph-memory and theorem publication protocols
Scott N. Armstrong Lean autoformalization workflow concepts: frozen public declarations, source dependency graph, binder/definition audit, OR-routes and post-proof cleanup
reuse_plan.decision_reason: Adapt the source-first ideas into BanditRLlib's existing zero-sorry, semantic-roundtrip and three-graph publication architecture rather than replacing that architecture or weakening existing gates.

semantic_roundtrip.verdict: not-required: this is a repository protocol/governance change and does not claim a new source theorem
semantic_roundtrip.remaining_semantic_delta: Future source-facing Anchors must implement the new Statement Seal, binder/definition audit, source-proof coverage and purification record in addition to the existing semantic round trip.

graph_contribution.functor_reason: The change defines graph truth contracts and a compressed-spine lifecycle but adds no theorem node, route milestone, or new conceptual transport.
graph_contribution.visual_review: Documentation-only protocol change; no generated graph layout is altered. README/news and protocol links should be inspected in rendered Markdown before merge.

website_surfaces: Repository News records the new Statement-Seal and Proof-Digestion protocol.

truth_boundary: This PR changes protocol and reader-compression requirements only. It does not retroactively certify old Source Proof Graph coverage, purify historical modules, prove any new Bandit/RL theorem, or claim that graph decomposition automatically measures scientific novelty.
